questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet of your current position.
Within 1,000 feet of your current position.
Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Always drive so you can stop completely within the distance you can see ahead of you if you need to.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard:

options.text: Do not brake because it can lock the wheels.
You should turn the wheel sharply.
You should hold the brakes down until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because it can lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: When turning to avoid a hazard, do not use the brakes while turning. Braking while turning can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: When driving a triple combination, keep the shut-off valves at the rear of the middle trailer:
questions.correctAnswerText: In the open position.
questions.explanation: When driving a double or triple combination, close the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. Keep all other shut-off valves open.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment if:
questions.correctAnswerText: They get too hot.
questions.explanation: Brakes can go out of adjustment quickly, especially if they overheat from heavy use. Check brake adjustment often.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol and driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Faster reaction time
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time and causes dangerous driving errors like drifting between lanes, failing to signal, running stop signs, and improper passing. Alcohol never improves reaction time.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Acceptable if you eat foods that are easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: A dangerous activity.
questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, and drinking distract you from driving and should be avoided. Plan ahead and stop to eat on long trips.

questions.question: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels:

options.text: Follow the same path as the front wheels.
Follow a different path than the front wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Longer vehicles have more off-tracking than shorter vehicles.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system. The air compressor governor controls the compressor.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may show that the driver is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that other drivers may be impaired, such as drinking too much, being tired, using drugs, or being sick. A driver with an open window in cold weather may be impaired.

questions.question: Most drivers are least alert:
questions.correctAnswerText: At night.
questions.explanation: Most people are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Tiredness and low alertness are major hazards when driving at night.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers. This alerts drivers behind you to your slow speed (if local laws allow flasher use).

questions.question: When checking tires, which of these is NOT a problem?

options.text: At least 4/32 inch of tread in the grooves on front tires
Using radial and bias-ply tires together

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 4/32 inch of tread in the grooves on front tires
questions.explanation: Check your tires for correct air pressure (not too low or too high), at least 4/32 inch of tread depth in every groove on front tires, and never mix radial and bias-ply tires.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase the space between your car and the car ahead. This reduces sudden moves and gives the tailgater room to pass. Do not speed up—this may cause the tailgater to follow even closer at the higher speed, creating more danger.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, what should you do?

options.text: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
Use any extinguisher on every type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
questions.explanation: Stay far away from the fire and aim your extinguisher at the base of the fire, not at the flames. For some fires, water may work better. If you are unsure, wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer will be easy to drive.
The vehicle will keep steering control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may swing around.
questions.explanation: If a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is more likely with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: When braking while pulling a trailer with anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Use extra braking force to make sure the brakes work.
Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving a trailer with an anti-lock braking system (ABS), brake normally. Do not change your braking technique because of the ABS.

questions.question: After a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right after the engine starts. If a light stays on, it means there is a problem with your vehicle.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine.
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine with gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic with a combination vehicle, it is especially important that you:

options.text: Make sure there is a large enough gap for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is a large enough gap for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Make sure there is enough gap in traffic before you enter or cross.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: On a vehicle with trailers, mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if the trailers are straight. Check mirrors before every trip.
